evidence.paraphrase: Valentin explains his method of following the unreasonable when no clue exists, reasoning that oddities noticed by pursuer and pursued may coincide.
evidence.quote: He said that if one had a clue this was the worst way; but if one had no clue at all it was the best, because there was just the chance that any oddity that caught the eye of the pursuer might be the same that had caught the eye of the pursued.

evidence.paraphrase: Valentin frames his questioning of the fruiterer as an inquiry into experimental psychology and association of ideas.
evidence.quote: "Pray excuse my apparent irrelevance, my good sir, but I should like to ask you a question in experimental psychology and the association of ideas."

evidence.paraphrase: Valentin lays out his tracking procedure: to mimic the movements of a target whose actions are unknown.
evidence.quote: "If you know what a man fffs doing, get in front of him; but if you want to guess what he fffs doing, keep behind him. Stray when he strays; stop when he stops; travel as slowly as he."

evidence.paraphrase: Valentin discovers the salt swapped for sugar, prompting his investigation of the anomaly.
evidence.quote: He had put salt in it.

evidence.paraphrase: Valentin systematically tests the containers to determine that sugar and salt have been deliberately swapped.
evidence.quote: He looked to see if there were any more orthodox vessels. Yes; there were two salt-cellars quite full. Perhaps there was some speciality in the condiment in the salt-cellars. He tasted it; it was sugar.

evidence.paraphrase: A detective reacts with disbelief at the seemingly senseless behavior of the men they are pursuing.
evidence.quote: the inspector said under his breath, "Are we after escaped lunatics?"

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts Valentin's ordinary holiday appearance with his concealed weapon, authority, and intellect.
evidence.quote: There was nothing about him to indicate the fact that the grey jacket covered a loaded revolver, that the white waistcoat covered a police card, or that the straw hat covered one of the most powerful intellects in Europe.

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown explains the reasoning behind his tests: normal reactions versus suppressed ones reveal a person with something to hide.
evidence.quote: "A man generally makes a small scene if he finds salt in his coffee; if he doesn fffffffffffffft, he has some reason for keeping quiet. I changed the salt and sugar, and you kept quiet. A man generally objects if his bill is three times too big. If he pays it, he has some motive for passing unnoticed. I altered your bill, and you paid it."

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown explains that he deliberately created memorable disturbances so the police could follow the trail.
evidence.quote: "as you wouldn fffffffffffffft leave any tracks for the police, of course somebody had to. At every place we went to, I took care to do something that would get us talked about for the rest of the day."

evidence.paraphrase: Valentin reacts with frustration while overhearing what seems to be innocent theological talk.
evidence.quote: Valentin behind his tree was tearing his fingernails with silent fury.

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown asserts that the laws of reason and morality hold universally even in imagined alien landscapes.
evidence.quote: "Reason and justice grip the remotest and the loneliest star."

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown reveals that Flambeau's disparagement of reason exposed him as not a real priest.
evidence.quote: "You attacked reason," said Father Brown. "It fffffffffffffffs bad theology."
